title: Working Out the Late Enrollment Penalty Taken Back Off a Ridgecrest RxSecure Account
content:
The late enrollment penalty taken back off a member's Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan account is the monthly penalty the relief is worked out on, multiplied by the coverage months whose penalty is being relieved, rounded to the nearest ten cents, and held to the ceiling the account allows.

## The three quantities that enter the figure

1. **The monthly penalty the relief is worked out on** is the figure the national base beneficiary premium and the plan's penalty rate give for the months without creditable coverage the enrollment carries. Both published figures are the ones certified for the plan held, and the count of uncovered months is the one the enrollment record carries.
2. **The coverage months whose penalty is relieved** are the coverage months the premium account has charged a penalty for in the 3 months up to the handling date, held down to the months the member's earlier coverage proves. The months the member's earlier coverage proves are the months without creditable coverage the enrollment carries.
3. **The ceiling** is the latest penalty charge the premium account carries; the relief never exceeds it.

## The order of the arithmetic

The multiplication is carried out first and its product rounded once to the nearest ten cents, and only that rounded product is then compared with the ceiling; no intermediate is rounded before it.

## Worked on hypothetical figures

Take a member whose enrollment carries 12 months without creditable coverage, whose premium account has charged a penalty for 3 coverage months in the 3 months up to the handling date, and on which the figure the published premium and rate give for those 12 uncovered months comes to a hypothetical 4.40 USD; take the latest penalty charge on the account to be a hypothetical 4.40 USD as well.

- The coverage months relieved are the lower of the 3 months the account has charged a penalty for in the window and the 12 months the member's earlier coverage proves, which is 3.
- The monthly penalty of 4.40 USD multiplied by those 3 months gives 13.20 USD, and rounding that product to the nearest ten cents leaves 13.20 USD.
- The ceiling is the latest penalty charge of 4.40 USD, and 13.20 USD exceeds it, so the amount taken back off is 4.40 USD.

Take the same member on a hypothetical account whose latest penalty charge is 22.00 USD instead. The rounded product of 13.20 USD is then below the ceiling, and the amount taken back off is 13.20 USD.

The member's own account of holding earlier drug coverage opens the enquiry and never fixes any of these figures.
